resources.string: Ripple talks to nearby phones directly over Bluetooth — no internet, no servers. It needs permission to scan for, advertise to and connect with nearby devices.
Public channel — reaches every phone in the mesh
End-to-end encrypted · relayed by the mesh
No peers yet. Keep Bluetooth on and bring another phone running Ripple within range.
Derived from a P-256 key generated on this device. Share it out-of-band to let others verify it\'s you.
Adds two fake peers (Asha, Ravi) so you can try the app with one phone. Ravi is two hops away and wanders out of range.
Only one phone? Try the simulated neighbourhood in Settings → Diagnostics

Ripple never uses the internet. Messages hop phone-to-phone over Bluetooth LE, are signed by the sender, and direct messages are end-to-end encrypted. Messages for peers who are out of range are held and delivered when the mesh reconnects.
Guided real-device checklist with an export ready for the field-test issue template
Mark each scenario as you go
Clear all verdicts and notes for this field-test run? The report has not been shared yet.
QR identity code, paste-import, pinned verified keys
Starting the mesh service… the identity code appears here in a moment.
QR code of your Ripple identity code
Scan this with any QR app (or copy/share the text) and hand the code to your contact over a channel you already trust. Ripple never uses the camera.
Paste the RIPPLE-ID:v1 code you received from them. The code is fully validated before anything is stored.
Not a valid Ripple identity code — check the prefix, lengths and hex, and paste it complete.
Safety code — read these digits to each other over any channel:
Equal digits on both phones mean you hold each other\'s real keys, not an impostor\'s.
That is your own identity code.
Key conflict: the mesh already knows a different key for this node id. Do NOT trust either until you resolve it in person — the pinned key is kept.
Pinned — this peer is now verified on this device.
Already pinned with the same key; record refreshed.
Refused: this node id is pinned to a different key. Your old pin was kept — talk to your contact before trusting either key.
No pinned peers yet. Import a peer\'s identity code above and pin it after comparing safety codes.
Pins live only in this app\'s private storage, alongside nothing secret (public keys) — but they are never logged. Un-pin only when your contact tells you their identity changed.
Encrypted identity blob so a reinstall keeps your node id
Whoever holds this code AND the passphrase is your identity — there is no revocation until Phase 2.2. Store it offline; a leaked passphrase means a lost identity.
The passphrase encrypts the export. It is never stored anywhere — a forgotten passphrase makes the backup permanently unreadable.
Could not create the blob — is the mesh service running?

This device still uses the legacy Keystore-only identity, whose key can never leave the hardware, so it cannot be exported. A restore on this device would move it onto the new backupable storage model.
QR code of your backup code
Keep the code and the passphrase in separate places (e.g. paper + memory). The QR is only a convenience for a nearby device.
Paste a RIPPLE-BKP:v1 code from any device of this identity. On a fresh install this rebuilds your exact node id and key.
Wrong passphrase — or the code was tampered with. No plaintext was recovered either way.
Not a valid Ripple backup code (check prefix, length and base64 body).

Heads-up: this differs from the identity currently in use on this device. Peers\' safety codes for you refer to your key — after restoring the SAME identity they stay valid; after restoring a DIFFERENT one, you are someone else to the mesh.
Restored. Restart Ripple to activate the identity.
Restore re-derives the node id and key from the blob, so old messages stay decryptable and other nodes keep verifying your signatures. No wire changes — this never leaves the app. See docs/BACKUP.md.
